claims.claim: The opt-in transport fixes the provider and model to Antigravity and gemini-3.8-flash and requires explicit effort.
The transport writes exact bounded request bytes to a temporary workspace, makes one bounded read-only native call, and removes the workspace after success or failure.
The transport shapes valid native output for JsonReviewerProvider and fails closed on invalid native output or process failure; the existing P3 protocol remains responsible for semantic validation.

Successful calls retain only immutable bounded usage and request-digest observations. The transport has no Executor adapter or Runtime dependency, and the offline composition tests check that provider attribution does not alter decision fingerprints.

The TASK-191 tests use injected runners and make no real provider call. All 16 failure cases retain their assertions; short deterministic IDs prevent the 262145-byte output case from expanding into a pytest node ID.
